trace.code: case RIGHT: p+=(ptrdiff_t) width*GetPixelChannels(image); q=p+step*(ssize_t) GetPixelChannels(image); for(i=0;i<width;i++){ p-=..; q-=..; if((size_t)(x_offset+width+step-i) > image->columns) continue; ... }

preconditions: An attacker supplies a crafted image and it is processed with a rotation or shear operation (-rotate / -shear / ShearRotateImage) at an angle whose per-row shear displacement `step` exceeds the available destination space `columns - x_offset - width`
The border computed by ShearRotateImage (bounds.x, which the same commit also fixes) is under-sized for the chosen dimensions/angle, so XShearImage is reached with an insufficient right-side padding
No privilege required: rotating/shearing a user-supplied image is a routine, unauthenticated operation in ImageMagick deployments (server-side image pipelines, CMS, CLI `magick`/`convert`)

evidence.vulnerable_version: ImageMagick 7.1.2-35 (2026-10-31) and all earlier releases; also master before 1360d45
evidence.fixed_version: unreleased on master only (1360d45, merged 2026-11-13); no release ships it (7.1.2-35 remains the newest tag)
evidence.observed_result: Differential against the verbatim-extracted XShearImage 'RIGHT' pixel-transfer loop (MagickCore/shear.c @ 1360d45~1). VULNERABLE: with columns=32,channels=4,x_offset=4,width=16,step=30 the trailing background fill writes columns [4..33]; columns 32 and 33 (8 Quantums) land past the 32-column pixel row and clobber the canary guard placed immediately after it (canary[0..7] overwritten with background/destination values). FIXED (upstream 1360d45): the up-front guard `if (step > columns - x_offset - width) break;` skips the row, no write reaches the canary. Marker printed: MAGICKOVERRUN-OK.

real_exploit.target: ImageMagick MagickCore/shear.c — the actual XShearImage() 'RIGHT' (right-to-left) pixel-transfer loop, extracted VERBATIM from commit 1360d45~1 (vendored under vendor/shear.c); the memory-safety-relevant pointer arithmetic, the insufficient in-loop guard, and the unguarded trailing background-fill writes are byte-for-byte identical to upstream
real_exploit.backend: the real vulnerable XShearImage loop compiled with zig cc, driven against a synthetic pixel row (32 columns x 4 channels of uint16 Quantums) followed by a contiguous canary guard region that models the heap memory immediately past the last row of the pixel cache
real_exploit.demonstrated: The pre-fix loop writes 8 Quantums (2 pixels) past the end of the pixel row, clobbering the canary (out-of-bounds WRITE, CWE-787). The same loop compiled with the upstream fix (1360d45's `if (step > columns - x_offset - width) break;` guard) skips the row entirely and leaves the canary intact. Impact demonstrated = attacker-controlled out-of-bounds write in the rotate/shear path that corrupts memory beyond the intended row/column boundary (adjacent pixel-cache rows/columns; and, for YShearImage's contiguous 1xrows column nexus buffer and the extreme-corner geometry, past the buffer allocation) — in ImageMagick's memory-unsafe C codebase the standard precondition for code execution.

evidence.notes: No public CVE/GHSA number is published yet, but the fix commit references GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-8xm2-q8hq-m68q (ImageMagick maintainer Dirk Lemstra, 2026-11-13, title 'Fixed possible out of bounds write in ShearRotateImage'). The fix is only on master; the newest release 7.1.2-35 (2026-10-31) predates it, so every released ImageMagick is still vulnerable. ShearRotateImage is the core of ImageMagick's `-rotate`/`-shear` (non-90-degree rotations), one of the most common image operations. The same commit also corrects the bounds.x border computation in ShearRotateImage (the geometry that can leave the right-side padding too small, making `step > columns - x_offset - width` reachable from a real rotate), and applies the analogous guard to YShearImage() 'DOWN' (bottom-to-top).
